items.question: Will FIDO publish AP2 as a standard, and when?
items.context: FIDO gave no deliverable or date when the work began on 2026-04-28. On 2026-09-08 its Payments Technical Working Group presented targets: harmonized AP2 and Verifiable Intent specifications by the end of 2026 and a first consolidated version in mid-2027. No public FIDO draft or repository for AP2 was found on 2026-11-21, and the GitHub repository has not changed since 2026-04-29.

items.question: What does Gemini's use of AP2 contain?
items.context: Google says Gemini has used AP2 for purchases since 2026-11-17, but names no AP2 version, mandate types, signer or verifier, and no source shows mandates reaching merchants, processors, Credential Providers or networks. The help page describes a browser and a possible virtual card number. The task settings (allowed merchants, a budget of up to $1000, an expiry within 14 days, optional confirmation) look like open-mandate constraints; that comparison is the atlas's own.

items.question: Will the reference SDK bind checkout_hash and transaction_id by default?
items.context: Issue 399 and fix PR 400 (2026-11-17) target the checkout chain verifier, which compares checkout_hash only when the caller passes the expected hash; the payment chain verifier treats transaction_id the same way. Both were open on 2026-11-21, and no commit has reached main since 2026-04-29.

items.question: How does a user withdraw an open mandate before exp?
items.context: v0.2 has no revocation; ERC-8226 shows an on-chain revoke and freeze for comparison.

items.question: Who keeps state for payment.budget and payment.agent_recurrence?
items.context: Both need history of earlier presentations, and the specification does not assign that role; Verifiable Intent calls such constraints network-enforced. A report of 2026-11-14 says the v0.2 samples keep those counters only on the agent's side.

items.question: How should a2a-x402 embed x402 in AP2 v0.2?
items.context: The documented Embedded Flow targets v0.1 CartMandate and PaymentMandate; no v0.2 mapping exists in either specification.

items.question: Can the context before signing be protected?
items.context: Research shows valid signatures do not prove intent when listings or tool results steer the agent; proposals bind credential lookups and cart lines to the session.

items.question: Will verifiers adopt consume-once semantics?
items.context: Runtime replay across retries is not covered; one paper proposes time-bound nonces and an issue reports that the samples never consume accepted mandates.

items.question: Which signature rule applies to the Checkout JWT?
items.context: The specification and the security considerations disagree on deterministic signatures; issue 268 is open and deferred to FIDO.

items.question: Will AP2 and Verifiable Intent converge on one set of key names?
items.context: Same vct values, different constraint prefixes, and Verifiable Intent renamed its keys on main without a version bump.

items.question: Will networks give mandate-backed transactions different liability?
items.context: AP2 leaves liability to the networks. Within Visa's system, Visa's rules (since 2025-10-18) make the cardholder responsible for an Agentic Payment Provider's actions; the rules yield to applicable law. Visa calls none of its agent rules a liability shift, and Worldpay (2026-07-30) says none exists yet for agent transactions. Issuers must still pay for Agentic Transactions made under cardholder instructions, and from 2026-10-24 a provider's login ID counts among the evidence in card-absent fraud disputes.
